Is there a reason why Eq is not defined as follows?

inductive Eq' {α : Sort u} (a : α) : α → Prop where
  | refl : Eq' a a

Note that Eq'.refl takes two implicit arguments while Eq.refl takes one implicit and one explicit argument.

As far as I understand, from the kernel's perspective there is no difference between implicit and explicit arguments, so in this sense the difference can't be fundamental. But is the difference important in the elaboration stage?

Well it's the difference between whether you write Eq.refl 1 or Eq.refl for 1 = 1. We already have rfl for the second variant so I guess refl takes an explicit as an alternative to rfl. Also, conventionally, refl is used as a name for the explicit variant and rfl for the implicit variant for a relation, take e.g. docs#Iff.refl, docs#Iff.rfl.
